sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *por más que* "however much, no matter how much" from B2 Unit 8. It takes the subjunctive when the effort or amount is open and does not change the result. The climate story of the Guna islands fits it well: however much people do, the sea keeps rising.

sections.title: Por más que and por mucho que
rows: Por más que se construyan muros, el mar seguirá subiendo.
However many walls are built, the sea will keep rising. (Open, general: subjunctive.)
Por mucho que cueste, algunas familias quieren irse.
However much it costs, some families want to leave.
Por muy seguras que sean las casas nuevas, dejar la isla es difícil.
However safe the new houses are, leaving the island is hard. (*por muy* + adjective + *que* + subjunctive.)
Por más que ampliaron la isla, el agua entraba en las casas.
However much they enlarged the island, the water came into the houses. (It really happened: indicative.)

items.spanish: Por más que bajen las emisiones, el nivel del mar seguirá subiendo durante décadas.
items.english: However much emissions fall, the sea level will keep rising for decades.

items.spanish: Por más que las casas nuevas sean seguras, para muchos es difícil dejar la isla.
items.english: However safe the new houses are, for many it is hard to leave the island.

items.spanish: Por mucho que cambie el clima, los guna quieren mantener su cultura.
items.english: However much the climate changes, the Guna want to keep their culture.

items.spanish: Por más que lo intentaron, no pudieron detener el agua.
items.english: However hard they tried, they could not stop the water.

sections.content: Use the subjunctive when you look ahead or speak in general (*por más que se construyan*), and the indicative when you tell what really happened (*por más que ampliaron*). The main clause often says that nothing changes: *no*, *seguirá*, *igual*.
